excerpts.author: gumb00
excerpts.content:
Re EOF constant stack height validation restriction: I have the following idea about making it less restricted.

- We use the old <@403707149043105803>  idea about "forward code restriction" (https://github.com/ipsilon/EIPs/pull/1), i.e. we require compilers to order the code blocks (inside a section) in a way that any block after terminating instruction (like e.g. helpers) is referenced by earlier _forward_ jump. This allows to do stack validation in one sequential pass over the code instead of using a worklist and following each jump like we do now.

- Instead of one stack_height value for each code position, we record the range (stack_height_min, stack_height_max) for each position.

- We treat backward and forward jumps differently:
  -  Backward jump still requires stack height of target to be constant - this should be fine restriction, because backwards jumps are normally used for loops, and loops won't be allowed to grow/shrink stack
  - Forward jumps to the same target are allowed to be from different stack heights and we update target's (stack_height_min, stack_height_max) on each forward jump.

Because validation is one sequential pass, by the time we reach jump target we know the real (min, max) stack range for it among all jumps.
